# WattSteer

> WattSteer predicts renewable curtailment on the Brazilian grid a day ahead,
> explains the grid conditions associated with it, and estimates how much of it
> storage or flexible demand could absorb.

WattSteer is a public, read-only site built on openly published data from ONS
(Operador Nacional do Sistema Elétrico), ANEEL and weather providers. It has no
accounts and no login.

## Pages

- [Home](https://wattsteer.com/): day-ahead curtailment risk by subsystem, the
  four engines behind it, and where the data comes from.
- [App](https://wattsteer.com/app): the product itself — Grid Overview,
  Explain, Mitigate and Time Machine.
- [Terms of Service](https://wattsteer.com/terms)
- [Privacy Policy](https://wattsteer.com/privacy)

## Notes

- Headline figures are quantiles, not point estimates. Every forecast is
  published as P10, P50 and P90; a figure shown without a band is a measured
  observation and is labelled as one.
- The four subsystems are NORTE, NORDESTE, SUL and SUDESTE/CENTRO-OESTE. A
  national figure is a derived sum over those four, never the ONS `SIN` row.
- Energy is reported in MWh. Money appears only as an explicitly labelled
  economic scenario, next to the R$/MWh it assumed. No carbon figure is
  claimed.
- Forecasts are modelled estimates carrying uncertainty, not operating
  instructions, trading signals or advice.
- Source data is published by third parties and is periodically revised; figures
  shown here can change. Metrics computed over windows that predate WattSteer's
  own ingestion are labelled revision-optimistic.
- Plant registry data is derived from ANEEL SIGA, © ANEEL, under the Open
  Database License (ODbL) v1.0; WattSteer's derived plant table is offered
  under the same licence.
- WattSteer is not affiliated with ONS or ANEEL.
